sentences.text: Shri Sankalp Kochar, learned counsel for the appellant.
Shri Santosh Yadav- Dy.G.A. appearing on behalf of Advocate General for the State.
Heard on admission.
Appeal being arguable, is admitted for final hearing.
Also heard on IA No.4531/2024, an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

A perusal of the judgment reveals that the appellant has been convicted under Section 342 of IPC and has been sentenced to undergo RI for 6 months with fine of Rs.500/- and under Section 376 (2)
(n) of the IPC and has been sentenced to undergo RI for ten years with fine of Rs.10,000/- with default stipulation.
Learned counsel for the appellant after extensively referring to deposition of prosecutrix (PW-1), her husband, son and other family members submits that prosecutrix is not a reliable witness.
Incident is said to have occurred in the intervening night of 02.12.2016 and 03.12.2016 but report has been lodged on 07.12.2016.
Thus, there is delay in lodging the first information report, for which, no explanation has been furnished.

Further, after referring to para 9 of prosecutrix's deposition, FSL report (Ex.P/6), deposition of Dr. Diksha Pandey (PW-12) and MLC prepared by her and also relying upon the order dated 01.07.2024 passed by co-ordinate Bench of this Court in M.Cr.C.No.51674/2022 (Major Amit Pathak Vs. State of M.P. and Anr.), it is 2 CRA-2437-2024 urged that in view of time gap between date of incident and medical examination of prosecutrix and para 9 of deposition of prosecutrix, FSL report Ex.P/6 is not reliable. Appellant is in jail since the date of judgment i.e. 09.02.2024.

sentences.text:
I have gone through the evidence on record and in view of nature of evidence available on record,
including medical evidence and delay in lodging the FIR, I deem it appropriate to suspend the jail sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, aforesaid I.A. is allowed.

Subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court with a further direction to appear before the concerning trial court on 25.10.2024 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
C. c. as per rules.
